analysis.investment_thesis: A tiny INR 68 Cr microcap seed company with a microscopic 0.57% ROE trading at 15.9x earnings — this is the definition of a fair-to-poor business at a rich price. Invert: the dominant outcome for a sub-1% ROE compounder is wealth destruction, not creation.
key_strengths: Operates in a structurally growing agri-inputs/seeds category
key_risks: ROE of 0.57% is catastrophic — capital earns less than a savings account
P/E 15.9 on near-zero earnings implies absurd P/B and valuation fragility
Microcap (INR 68 Cr) in a commoditised seed business with no visible moat
red_flags: ROE <1% — fails every basic quality test
Recent 2016 vintage with no long-term earnings track record as a listed entity
Valuation disconnected from return on capital economics
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Unisem Agritech earns 0.57% on equity. Let that number sink in — a fixed deposit dominates this business. Paying 15.9x earnings for such returns means buying at a very high price-to-book against a capital base that doesn't compound. The seed industry can be reasonable (think Kaveri Seed's former days), but that economics requires genetics/IP moats and scale, neither of which is demonstrated here by a 2016-founded microcap.

The only positive signal is promoter holding at 70.88%, but alignment without capability is worthless — I want owners who are both honest AND able to earn >15% on capital. The Munger checklist (ROIC >15%, earnings quality, durable moat, understandable economics) fails on virtually every dimension. Pass decisively and move to the "too hard" pile.
